Back: Reflection is Java's ability to inspect and interact with classes, methods, fields, constructors, and annotations at runtime.

Front: What does Class<?> represent, and how can you obtain it?
Back: Class<?> is the runtime representation of a Java type. Common ways: MyClass.class, object.getClass(), and Class.forName("...").

Front: What is the difference between getMethods() and getDeclaredMethods()?
Back: getMethods() returns public methods, including inherited ones. getDeclaredMethods() returns methods declared in the class, including non-public methods.

Front: Why must an annotation use RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME to be read with reflection?
Back: Only RUNTIME-retained annotations remain available while the program is running, so reflection can discover them with isAnnotationPresent() and getAnnotation().

Front: Why do frameworks such as Spring use reflection, and what are the main tradeoffs?
Back: Reflection enables dynamic discovery, inspection, and invocation of application classes. Tradeoffs include reduced compile-time safety, more runtime errors, more complexity, and possible runtime overhead.
